purpose: Darifenacin is used to treat overactive bladder. It helps reduce the sudden, strong urge to urinate, cuts down on how often you need to go to the bathroom, and helps prevent accidental leakage of urine. It is especially helpful if you feel like you can't always make it to the bathroom in time.
how_it_works: Your bladder has special receptors that can cause it to squeeze too often or too suddenly. Darifenacin works by blocking those receptors, which helps calm the bladder muscle down. Think of it like putting the brakes on an overactive bladder so it doesn't squeeze when it's not supposed to.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is constipation, which can affect many people taking this medication. You may also notice a dry mouth, blurry vision, dry eyes, stomach upset, or difficulty fully emptying your bladder. Drinking plenty of water and eating fiber-rich foods can help with constipation.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, trouble urinating, a blockage in your stomach or intestines, or liver problems, as this medication may not be right for you. Avoid driving or using heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, since it can sometimes cause blurry vision or dizziness. Tell your pharmacist about all other medications you take, because many drugs can interact with darifenacin. Do not crush or chew the tablet — swallow it whole.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is one 7.5 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day. After two weeks, your doctor may increase your dose to 15 mg once a day if needed. Take it at the same time each day, with or without food, and swallow the tablet whole without crushing or chewing it.
